3 Apologies and Leave of Absence
Cr Kerry Morton has advised the Mayor and CEO that he was unable to attend this meeting.
Minute No. 2024.08.19-OM-01
Moved Cr Clarke and Seconded Cr Watson
That Council accept the apology submitted by Cr Morton.
                                                                              Carried 4/0


4 Acknowledgement of Country
Mayor Cr Francis Murray acknowledged the Wangkamadla People, Traditional Custodians of
the land on which we meet today and paid respect to their Elders, past and present. He
extended that respect to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people here today.


5 Condolences
Condolences are extended to Cr Morton and his family on the passing of his mother, Mrs
Beverly Morton OAM.
Our thoughts go out to the Morton family. Bev was an extraordinary person who touched the
lives of everyone in the Diamantina community. She will be dearly missed, but her memory
will always be cherished and fondly remembered.
The meeting observed a minute’s silence, as a mark of respect.




Agenda Ordinary Council Meeting Monday 16 September 2024                            Page 5

interest in Agenda item 12.4.3.

12.1.2 Engineer’s Report - GBA

Cooling Ponds Project, Part of Lot 14 SP303311


Attendance – Morning tea adjournment at 11.11am. The meeting resumed at 11.27am.


12.1.2 Engineer’s Report - GBA (continued)

Cooling Ponds Project, Part of Lot 14 SP303311

That having regard to:

    (a) advice that the Department of Resources (“Department”) has decided that native title
        is already extinguished by way of a public works previous exclusive possession act
        (“PEPA”) over that part of the Birdsville township reserve required for the Cooling
        Ponds Project (“Project Area”);
    (b) clause 34.2 of the registered Indigenous Land Use Agreement (“ILUA”) over the
        Project Area to which Council is party, provides that the parties agree and will not
        dispute extinguishment within the ILUA area by way of PEPA; and
    (c) the Department’s advice that a deed of grant in fee simple (“freehold grant”), will be
        offered to Council over the Project Area on revised terms to the in-principle offer
        previously made.


Minute No. 2024.08.19-OM-05
Moved Cr Watson and Seconded Cr Dare


That Council makes the following decisions:



Agenda Ordinary Council Meeting Monday 16 September 2024                                 Page 7
    1. Any revised offer of the kind referred to in paragraph (c) above, be accepted
       provided its terms are considered reasonable by the Chief Executive Officer.
    2. Council and its agents and contractors make best endeavours to work with the
       Department to secure the making by the State of the freehold grant before the
       Queensland Government enters the upcoming caretaker period.
    3. Council delegates authority to the Chief Executive Officer to formally accept
       any revised offer of a freehold grant, and take all such measures necessary for
       that purpose, in accordance with this resolution.
                                                                             Carried 4/0

12.4.3 Bedourie Race Track Earthworks
Cr Dare declared a prescribed conflict of interest in this matter, given he is an office bearer
of the Bedourie Amateur Race Club Incorporated. Councillor Dare dealt with the conflict by
leaving the meeting and taking no part in the decision-making process.
Attendance - Cr Dare left the meeting at 5.53pm.
Cr Watson declared a declarable conflict of interest in this matter, given he is a member of
the Bedodurie Amateur Race Club Incorporated. Cr Watson recognised that although he
had a declarable conflict of interest, he would reasonably be perceived to be impartial
because he is not an office bearer. Cr Watson stated that he wished to remain in the meeting
and he requested eligible councillors to decide if he may participate in the debate and
decision-making despite his declarable conflict of interest.



Agenda Ordinary Council Meeting Monday 16 September 2024                                  Page 15
The eligible councillors present were Crs Murray and Clarke.


Minute No. 2024.08.19-OM-29
Moved Cr Murray and Seconded Cr Clarke
That Cr Watson be permitted to remain in the meeting, participate in the debate and
subsequent decision-making regarding agenda item 12.4.3 which pertains to
proposed Bedourie Race Track earthworks. The eligible Councillors make this
decision based upon Cr Watson’s indication that he can be impartial and that he is an
ordinary member of the Bedourie Amateur Race Club Incorporated, and not an office
bearer.
                                                                               Carried 2/0

Moved Cr Clarke and Seconded Cr Murray

Minute No. 2024.08.19-OM-42
Moved Cr Watson and Seconded Cr Dare
1. That the Selection Panel Report (attached) on the process undertaken, outcome of
   applications and interviews conducted for appointment to the position of Chief
   Executive Officer (CEO) for Diamantina Shire Council be received and noted.


2. That the preferred candidate who was selected following the CEO Recruitment
   Panel’s final deliberations held after receiving the full Council’s feedback on the
   final presentations and interviews conducted on Wednesday 17 July and then
   again across the week commencing Monday 5 August 2024, be offered the
   position of Chief Executive Officer of Diamantina Shire Council.


3. That the Mayor, in consultation with the Recruitment Consultants, be authorised to
   negotiate and finalise the appointment based on the following terms and
   conditions:
      a. A four (4) year performance-based contract;
      b. A total remuneration package of up to $280,000 being the total value of
          components of remuneration offered, including base salary,
          superannuation and the private use value of the Council provided motor
          vehicle;
      c. A relocation allowance be offered if required up to a limit of $15,000 to
          cover the cost of relocating household and other items, subject to 50% of
          the reimbursement being paid on relocation and the remaining 50% after 12
          months satisfactory service as assessed by the Performance Review Panel;
      d. The policies of the Council which grant an entitlement to the employee
          relating to the private use of the Council motor vehicle, the incidental
          private use of the Council provided mobile phone and laptop computer, and
          the relocation allowance be included in a Schedule annexed to the
          Contract.


4. That no public announcement of the name of the successful candidate be made
   until such time as the Mayor has obtained a written acceptance of the offer from
   the preferred candidate.


5. That the independent Recruitment Consultants complete the agreed suite of
   background checks on the preferred candidate and the offer is subject to
   satisfactory return of same.

   considerations in respect of the Chief Executive Officer recruitment process.

OPERATIONAL UPDATE
Facilities
Message from Facilities team – We have been Fencing Houses in Bedourie. Trenching at
the Racecourse for 11 replaced power poles (Caravan Park Style) with water taps installed
in the competitors camping area, Costs for this work, Quote from electrician $37,266.02, and
council cost for the trenching labour and plant is $11,626.73, the old ones were a safety
hazard as in the past we have had them arcing out and sparks falling onto camps when
raining due to the birds chewing the lines, we had to have electricians do patch ups to help
sort this out, we were also having a lot of cut outs and need of a generator to assist with
power outlets. A new enclosure for gas bottles at kitchen, safety requirement. General
maintenance of both towns’ inspections for future projects. Co-ordinated works with
Electricians and Plumbers.
Plumber Position is still vacant. HR still has it advertised. A conversation has been had in
regards to possibly changing the outlook of filling this position. Possible casual position for
travellers to help fill the role and get feet on the ground to try and complete some tasks, not
only plumbing.
DABFAB industries and Chapo’s Plumbing Pty Ltd are currently doing the required plumbing
for Council

      •   Pricing installation of more water taps in the camping area of the bronco branding
          area in Birdsville.
      •   Request for quotes for 11 and 13 Jardine Street for an upgrade to the septic lines
          from the houses, on recent inspection after considerable request from the tenant
          regarding toilet issues it has been noted 13 Jardine Street has started to sink which
          has made the line from the house to the septic block up as it is not going downhill. 11
          Jardine Street is on the same line.
Electricians BAE and Outback Power have both been coordinated to do tasks that are on the
maintenance list.

ATTACHMENTS
Letter of Recommendation – Supply and Install Cooling Pond Liner



PURPOSE
To outline the procurement, assessment and award of the Supply and Installation of Cooling
Pond Liner for the new cooling pond in Birdsville.


OFFICER RECOMMENDATION
That Council accept Geotest Pty Ltd for the Supply and Installation of Cooling Pond Liner for
$ 286,733.66 excluding GST.



REPORT
Background
Tender documents for the supply and installation of cooling pond liner were uploaded to
Vendorpanel on June 7, 2024, and one was also emailed out.
Tenders closed 2pm, August 23, 2024, with two submissions received via Vendorpanel and
three received by email.
    1.   Geotest Pty Ltd
    2.   Merit Lining Systems
    3.   Simon Hullock
    4.   Fabtech
    5.   Curtis Barrier Intl Pty Ltd


Discussion/Current Issue




Agenda Ordinary Council Meeting Monday 16 September 2024                                       Page 42
CONSIDERATIONS/IMPLICATIONS
Corporate/Operational Plan Reference/Policy/Legislation
Our Infrastructure is constructed and maintained in a sustainable manner which meets
community needs.
Our Infrastructure guarantees quality potable urban water supply and wastewater treatment.
Secure potable water sources are maintained for Bedourie and Birdsville.
Budget/Financial/Resourcing
Tendered submission for Geotest Pty Ltd $ 286,733.66 excluding GST.
$4 million allocated in 2024/25 Budget, works order 2463 in Cooling Pond Construction Liner
Pipework hex power.
Communication/Engagement
Nil


Risk Assessment
The final size of the cooling pond will need to be determined which may result in additional
lining costs.


Timings/Deadline
The works can’t commence until the earthworks are completed.


Conflict of Interest Declaration
Nil


Human Rights Impact
Human Rights are not impacted.


Alternatives Considered
The alternative lining options include importing clay materials or bentonite products, moisture
conditioning/ spreading and compaction. This is a labour intensive and time consuming
activity and may result in leaks which would require draining of the pond and reapplication of
clay/bentonite products potentially several times before a water tight seal is obtained. The
PE welded liner is cheaper and more reliable and is proven technology.

                                         markets.

For this project it states that the HDPE will need to with stand water temperature 98deg C. Is it just the initial water entry
temperature or will 98 deg C be the constant temperature for this cooling pond?


This information is required for HDPE material decision-making.


Thanks.

ANSWER (Public) on 24/Jul/2024 02:39 PM : Good Afternoon,


The cooling pond water is expected to run between 25 and 55 degrees. The pond will initially be filled with cooled water at
around 30 degrees.

Can you please provide commentary on the below items:


1. What grade of geotextile is required to be installed underneath the HDPE geomembrane?
2. The proposed Supplier "Industial Plastics'" HDPE material is based on a GRI-GM13 specification. Will Council accept
material supplied from other Supplier's that will meet the GRI-GM13 specification?
3. Is the HDPE geomembrane smooth on both sides?
4. In the absence of Project Specifications, are there any independent material test requirements.

ANSWER (Public) on 24/Jul/2024 04:39 PM : Afternoon,
1. What grade of geotextile is required to be installed underneath the HDPE geomembrane?
A protective cushion geofabric to protect the liner such as Bidim Strength Class A.


2. The proposed Supplier "Industial Plastics'" HDPE material is based on a GRI-GM13 specification. Will Council accept
material supplied from other Supplier's that will meet the GRI-GM13 specification?
Yes


3. Is the HDPE geomembrane smooth on both sides?
This will depend on the product to be supplied


4. In the absence of Project Specifications, are there any independent material test requirements.
No however the proposed products will be assessed as part of the submission


5. Given the scope, its taken that the earthwork preparation of the pond will be done by others and handed over to the
Linings Company to progress with the trench excavation and liner works.
Correct


6. Are there any test requirements from Council for the mass concrete?
No


7. Will flights in- and out of Birdsville including accommodation and messing be provided by yourselves free of charge?
No

Geotest
As well as being involved in the design and installation of geomembrane liners and floating covers,
Geotest Pty Ltd works collaboratively with other Geomembrane Installation Companies, Contractor’s,
Consulting Engineers and Principals to provide services to assure the performance of installed
geomembranes through the auditing of materials, advice on long term performance issues, and
inspection and electrical survey testing of geomembranes post installation throughout Australia.

Geotest provides solutions within the mining, oil & gas, landfill, agricultural, potable water storage
and wastewater sectors. Our clients include various international and local companies, government
and private utility providers and local councils.

Our services cover a range of applications, including, but not limited to, landfill liners, industrial
storage ponds, wastewater treatment membranes, potable water storage basins, tank installations,
methane collection covers, dam drainage systems and tunnels.

Geotest is the only Installation Company in Australia that has an in-house Design Department,
managed by a Chartered Professional Engineer with 8 years industry experience specialized in
different applications.

Please find our full Capability Statement, attached.

Geotest’s Quality Strategy
Geotest is a geomembrane company specialised in Design, RLI Testing, Material Review, Auditing, CQA,
CQC, Training, and generally undertakes project installations which require a high level of quality with
documented compliance.
In addition to installing approximately 1,000,000m2 of materials we have a substantial database of
projects (in excess of 20,000,000m2) that have been integrity tested. This data allows Geotest to
analyse, research and implement quality improvements. This experience has shown that the only way
to achieve the highest possible quality standards is to build quality into the entire construction process.

Geotest Australia’s quality processes deliver a very high rate of tested and documented zero defect
projects. Attempting to inspect quality into an inadequate construction process cannot achieve this
outcome.



Geotest Credentials
Geotest has extensive experience constructing lining systems for critical storages and can
demonstrate a history of successful projects with a variety of blue-chip clients throughout the mining
and resources sector. Geotest have undertaken numerous geomembrane supply and installation
projects for Clients in a variety of Sectors. Should you require further information regarding our
capabilities in this regard please don’t hesitate to contact us.

              Electric Leak Survey
                 Geotest is the market leader in electrical leak detection having completed testing of over ten
                 million square meters of geomembrane. With extensive research and development, we have
                 created the most sensitive and sophisticated electrical leak testing equipment in Australia.
                 Electrical leak detection is a method used to identify leaks or defects in geomembranes by applying
                 electrical testing techniques to find and locate potential breaches in the liner.

                  Although it is not a specified project requirement, Geotest is committed to delivering the
                  highest standards of quality and safety. As such, we will perform an Electrical Leak
                  Survey of the completed lining installation at no additional cost to the client. This
                  proactive measure is designed to enhance the overall quality of the installation and

ATTACHMENTS
Letter of Recommendation – Supply and Install Cooling Pond Equipment



PURPOSE
To outline the procurement, assessment and award of the Supply and Installation of Cooling
Pond Equipment for the old cooling pond as a risk mitigation measure for the failing copper
pipework.
OFFICER RECOMMENDATION
That Council accept the tender from Dab Fab Industrial for the Supply and Installation of
Cooling Pond Equipment is accepted for $ 266,063.85 excluding GST.



REPORT
Background
Tender documents for the supply and installation of cooling pond equipment were uploaded
to Vendorpanel on July 18, 2024.
Tenders closed 2pm, August 13, 2024, with two submissions received.
    1. Complex Civil Infrastructure Services Pty Ltd
    2. Dab Fab Industrial
Discussion/Current Issue
The submerged copper pipework system in the cooling pond has reached the end of life.
The new cooling pond system wont be online for 12-18 months and a contingency is
required to ensure cooled water for residents of Birdsville is available. This equipment will be
installed in the old cooling pond to replace the submerged copper pipework.


CONSIDERATIONS/IMPLICATIONS



Agenda Ordinary Council Meeting Monday 16 September 2024                                       Page 76
Corporate/Operational Plan Reference/Policy/Legislation
Our Infrastructure is constructed and maintained in a sustainable manner which meets
community needs.
Our Infrastructure guarantees quality potable urban water supply and waste water treatment.
Secure potable water sources are maintained for Bedourie and Birdsville
Budget/Financial/Resourcing
Tendered submission for Dab Fab Industrial $ 266,063.85 excluding GST.
$4 million allocated in 2024/25 Budget, works order 2463 in Cooling Pond Construction Liner
Pipework hex power.
Communication/Engagement
Nil
Risk Assessment
The site is complex and aging and the works are difficult to scope accurately to contractors
who are not familiar with the site. Dab Fab Industrial are familiar with the site and have
undertaken a range of different tasks at this site which should minimize the potential for
variations.
Timings/Deadline
The Heat Exchanger has arrived in Birdsville so works can commence in the near future.
The copper pipework is likely to fail again in the short term.
Conflict of Interest Declaration
Nil
Human Rights Impact
Human Rights will not be impacted
Alternatives Considered
The original submerged galvanised pipework and the subsequent copper pipework
represents older technology that has limited effectiveness in cooling hot bore water.
Corrosion issues have plagued both systems with leaks reducing the effectiveness of the
submerged pipework and also the heat exchanger (as the cool pond reservoir is warmer
because of the leaks). The plate heat exchanger is easier to maintain/ replace and will
ensure a cooler reservoir of pond water that will be more effective at cooling the bore water.

Business Overview:                       Diamantina consists of two main towns Birdsville and Bedourie, with a third town of
                                         Betoota.

                                         Bedourie is located 1,600km west of Brisbane, while Birdsville is 200km south of Bedourie
                                         and 1,200km from Adelaide.

                                         Our towns have four aircraft services per week on the Brisbane- Mount Isa Circuit. REX
                                         (Regional Express) provides this service.

                                         Despite it's size, Birdsville is a well-known destination for many Australian and
                                         International visitors. The town hosts one horse race meeting a year, when over 6,000
                                         people swell the town population. It is the start of the famous Birdsville Track, which
                                         originally was used as a stock route for moving cattle from Queensland to Southern
                                         markets.

                                         Bedourie is the Shire's administration centre. The last ten years has seen its population
                                         more than double to 140 people. The town boasts many new amenities including an
                                         aquatic centre, hot artesian spa and a community hall. Visitor numbers have increased to
                                         over 120,000 per year.

                                         The Shire's wealth lies within its cattle industry, tourism and natural environment. Located
                                         within Queensland's Channel Country, bordering South Australia and the Northern
                                         Territory, this area is renown for producing prime quality beef. The natural irrigation from
                                         the Diamantina and Georgina River Systems is also assisting with developing an organic
                                         cattle industry.

                                         We are fortunate that National Parks comprise 25% of our shire's area. The Simpson
                                         Desert, Diamantina National Park, (just been named in the top ten National Parks in
                                         Australia) and Astrebla National Park all offer unique scenery and wildlife for visitors to
                                         experience.

                                         Visit the Diamantina Shire for a unique outback experience.

PURPOSE
To seek approval for the Works for Queensland funding allocations.
OFFICER RECOMMENDATION
That Council endorses the 2024-2027 Works For Queensland Program Scope of Works as
the following:
    - $100,000 Betoota Showgrounds Shed for the Betoota Race Club Inc./ Betoota
         Gymkhana Club/ Betoota Social Club
    - $100,000 Bronco branding yards amenities and kitchen for the Birdsville Social Club
    - $200,000 Bedourie Showgrounds Awning for the Bedourie Amateur Race Club
    - $80,000 Birdsville Cemetery fencing
    - $80,000 Bedourie Cemetery Fencing
    - $960,000 Bedourie & Birdsville town street Reseals


REPORT
Background
The Department of Housing, Local Government, Planning and Public Works is responsible
for administering the 2024-27 Works for Queensland funding round (2024-27 W4Q). Council
has been allocated $1,520,000 to deliver local projects that create jobs, deliver better
services, and improve the lives of Queenslanders now and into the future. All works must be
completed by 30 June 2027. The online application process was completed before closing
on 5 July 2024 based upon feedback from budget workshops.

TC2024001 Letter of Recommendation – Diamantina Betterment 2023 Event



PURPOSE

To outline the procurement, assessment and award of the Diamantina Betterment 2023
Event Tender.
OFFICER RECOMMENDATION
That Council resolves to accept the tender for $ 339,636.00 excluding GST, submitted by
Mann Made Construction for the Diamantina Betterment 2023 program, for the construction
of concrete floodways.

REPORT
Background
In late July 2024, the funding agreement was signed with the Queensland Reconstruction
Authority for the approved Betterment submission under the Northern and Central
Queensland Monsoon and Flooding, 20 December 2022 – 30 April 2023 event to construct
three floodways. The three concrete floodways will be located on the Betoota - Mooraberree
Road chainage 0.276, Diamantina Lakes—Winton Boundary Road chainage 26.882, and
Springvale—Boulia Shire Boundary Road chainage 28.87. The concrete floodways are 20-
22m long to be completed under this contract. Council crews or local contractors will
complete the approach earthworks and side track construction.




Agenda Ordinary Council Meeting Monday 16 September 2024                                      Page 116
On 2 August 2024 tender documents for the TC2024001 Diamantina Betterment 2023 were

6. War (Nq) Pty Ltd

include Councils costs to complete the side track works and approach gravel works to tie
into the new floodway.

Business Overview:                       Diamantina consists of two main towns Birdsville and Bedourie, with a third town of
                                         Betoota.

                                         Bedourie is located 1,600km west of Brisbane, while Birdsville is 200km south of Bedourie
                                         and 1,200km from Adelaide.

                                         Our towns have four aircraft services per week on the Brisbane- Mount Isa Circuit. REX
                                         (Regional Express) provides this service.

                                         Despite it's size, Birdsville is a well-known destination for many Australian and
                                         International visitors. The town hosts one horse race meeting a year, when over 6,000
                                         people swell the town population. It is the start of the famous Birdsville Track, which
                                         originally was used as a stock route for moving cattle from Queensland to Southern
                                         markets.

                                         Bedourie is the Shire's administration centre. The last ten years has seen its population
                                         more than double to 140 people. The town boasts many new amenities including an
                                         aquatic centre, hot artesian spa and a community hall. Visitor numbers have increased to
                                         over 120,000 per year.

                                         The Shire's wealth lies within its cattle industry, tourism and natural environment. Located
                                         within Queensland's Channel Country, bordering South Australia and the Northern
                                         Territory, this area is renown for producing prime quality beef. The natural irrigation from
                                         the Diamantina and Georgina River Systems is also assisting with developing an organic
                                         cattle industry.

                                         We are fortunate that National Parks comprise 25% of our shire's area. The Simpson
                                         Desert, Diamantina National Park, (just been named in the top ten National Parks in
                                         Australia) and Astrebla National Park all offer unique scenery and wildlife for visitors to
                                         experience.

                                         Visit the Diamantina Shire for a unique outback experience.

12.1.7 DECISION ACTION REPORTS


Director Infrastructure Services
Feasibility study to decarbonise isolated communities Update and Background
 DECISION REPORT

 Date: 12/08/2024                                  Presentation Duration: Approx 15 minutes
 To:                                               General Council Meeting
 Author:                                           Stuart Bourne
 Authorising Officer:                              Bob Stephen, Director of Infrastructure Services
 File Reference:            InfoExpert -
 Presented for:             Information


ATTACHMENTS
Nil
PURPOSE

To provide an update on the rooftop solar trial undertaken with Ergon Energy.
OFFICER RECOMMENDATION

For information only.



REPORT
Background
In 2019, on the back of the closure of the Birdsville Geothermal power station operated by
Ergon, Council and Ergon Energy commenced discussions to collaboratively seek out
options for economic power supply to the towns of Bedourie and Birdsville.
Because both towns are not connected to the national grid, power is sourced from diesel
generators running 24 hours per day at a power station located in each town.
In early 2020 Bedourie and Birdsville joined a feasibility study with Ergon Energy into how
new technologies such as smart communication devices can be used to transition remote
communities towards renewable power generation and reduce the reliance on diesel
generators. Planning, design and procurement activities were undertaken with works
commencing in November 2020. The project was funded by Building Our Regions Round 5
($944,860 BoR, $128,904 Council).
The installation of inverters and solar panels was completed in six months (May 2021).
However, the units were not immediately operational as upgrade works were required by
Ergon to the power stations in both towns. The Bedourie power station was upgraded in
August 2021 and the Birdsville power station was upgraded in March 2021. Testing /
Commissioning commenced at these times in each town. A number of issues emerged
during the commissioning phase which caused ongoing delays due to troubleshooting and
implementing corrective actions.




Agenda Ordinary Council Meeting Monday 16 September 2024                                      Page 179
The system involves the Ergon power station curtailing individual rooftop solar sites from
producing power to ensure network stability. For example when it is sunny and little power is
being used by the town the power station curtails the rooftop solar to ensure no excess
power is being generated, which would threaten the stability of the network. This results in
rooftop solar ramping up and down throughout the day to suit the power demand of the town.




        Ergon




                                                           SwitchDin



                                                                                       TSC /
                                                                                       Council
                                                                       SGD Supplied
                                                                       by Ergon via
                                                                       SwitchDin for
                                                                       TSC install


A number of issues have been encountered and addressed since commissioning:
    -    Communication timing out or dropping out requiring manual device reset
    -    Communication congestion, so many devices trying to communicate via the SGD to
         the power station, firmware update rolled out to reduce polling
    -    Inverter configurations/ settings incorrect or had to be changed (powerfactors)
    -    Inability to access some inverters remotely (tunnelling)
    -    Firmware updates to inverters and secure gateway devices sometimes requiring
         additional software patches to be written and rolled out to maintain the
         communication between the devices
    -    Some SGD firmware updates causing dropouts requiring manual resetting
    -    Some inverter firmware updates causing dropouts requiring manual resetting or
         changing configurations/ settings which had to be reset
    -    Additional code to be prepared and updated to allow automatic overnight reboot
    -    The SwitchDin dashboard which displays the status of the sites has been improved
         to make troubleshooting easier
    -    Some setting changes aren’t being saved correctly by the inverters – needs to be
         done multiple times
    -    Some inverters not registered with SMA preventing firmware updates



Agenda Ordinary Council Meeting Monday 16 September 2024                               Page 180
      -   SGD continual setting changes for the inverter for the MPPT (Max power point
          tracker) which adjusts impedance to suit the power requirement. They are supposed
          to be designed to do this but possibly it is set too frequently, resulting in the MPPT
          getting ‘stuck’ on very low/no resistance
      -   A power reticulation issue at Bedourie under low loads – due to reactive reverse flow.
          Not to do with Solar but caused by the network. Change fixed power factor on
          inverters.
      -   The main issue was the NSS Quickstop (SMA error code) which is part of the
          communication between the SMA inverters and the Ergon Power station via the SGD
          – turns off the AC relay on the inverter without turning off the DC – results in burn
          out/short of the capacitor on DC side. The affected units have been replaced under
          warranty.
      -   Sim card failures (to be replaced)
      -   Data consumption was very high resulting in high Telstra costs. The polling frequency
          has been reduced cutting the data consumption in half.



Discussion/Current Issue
The current issues involve monitoring of the dashboard and troubleshooting on an as
required basis. This generally involves resetting units identified or possibly further
investigations such as replacement sim cards or raising a ticket with SwitchDin for further
investigation.


CONSIDERATIONS/IMPLICATIONS
The overall system is complex and susceptible to many different types of potential failures.
Close ongoing monitoring and troubleshooting will be required to maintain the system.
Corporate/Operational Plan Reference/Policy/Legislation
Our Environment Benefits from the utilisation of renewable energy sources.
Our Community has a cost of living in the comparable to South East Queensland.
Our Community has access to a reliable and affordable renewable electricity supply.


Budget/Financial/Resourcing
An annual allocation will be required to monitor and troubleshoot sites that are down.
Communication/Engagement
Nil
Risk Assessment
Nil
Timings/Deadline
Nil
Conflict of Interest Declaration
Nil
Human Rights Impact




Agenda Ordinary Council Meeting Monday 16 September 2024                                 Page 181
Nil
Alternatives Considered
It is likely that this model won’t be further replicated in other remote sites by Ergon. An
alternative model involving a solar farm located adjacent to the power station could easily be
controlled with fewer communications issues and less stakeholders. The disadvantage of
this alternative model is that any savings are unlikely to be passed onto residents.

CONDITIONS OF REQUEST FOR TENDER FOR THREE (3) NEW OR USED FLAT TOP SEMI -
TRAILERS AND TWO (2) NEW OR USED DOLLIES, TANDEM - SPRING.
1.1 Request for Tender Documents
      A. The Organisation providing the Tender shall complete all details on the Tender
         Form which shall be recognised as the Tender.
      B. The Organisation providing the Tender shall sign the Tender or if the
         Organisation is a corporation, affix the common seal or otherwise formally sign
         the Tender.
      C. Selection shall be made from the signed Tender and not from any literature or
         letter accompanying the Tender, unless such attachments are specifically
         referred to in the signed Tender Schedule.


1.2 Variations from Specification
      A. If because of the basic design or other factors it is impracticable for the
           organisation providing the Tender to fully comply with the specifications of the
           equipment required, he/she shall clearly list these variations and attach to the
           General Request for Tender Schedule.
      B. Unless these exclusions are stated, it shall be expected that the trailers offered
           comply with the specification in all respects.


1.3 Time for Delivery
       A. The organisation providing the Tender shall state on the tender the time for
          delivery of the trailers. A monetary penalty shall be incurred by the successful
          organisation on failure to comply with the stated time, and at Council discretion.
          The penalty shall be calculated at the rate of 0.1% of the Tender price per
          ordinary working day, i.e., Monday to Friday, exclusive of public holidays, that
          the actual delivery time exceeds the stated delivery time. Council also reserves
          the power to subtract this calculated penalty amount from the Tender price and
          to make payment accordingly.
       B. Delivery shall be to the Council Depot at Eyre Street, Bedourie, and the supplying
          organisation should nominate the price involved in delivering the item to this
          point in their Tender price. If the successful organisation/supplier fails to supply
          the vehicles or equipment quoted within the time set out in their Tender
          document, Council reserves the right to cancel the order and either place an
          order with another organisation/supplier or recall Tenders.


1.4 Lodgement of Tender
    A. The Tender must be lodged through the Vendor panel system.

      D. If the successful organisation fails to supply the trailers quoted on within the time as

         either place an order with another organisation or recall the quotations.

12.1.10           INFORMATION REPORT
Bullrushes, Birdsville Billabong
 Directorate:                             Infrastructure
 Date:                                    12/09/2024
 To:                                      Ordinary Council Meeting
 Author:                                  Bob Stephen Director Infrastructure
 Authorising Officer:                     Scott Mason, Interim Chief Executive Officer
 File Reference:                          IX


OFFICER RECOMMENDATION
That Council receive the report and that those matters not covered by resolution be noted.


ATTACHMENTS
    1.    Elders Email
OPERATIONAL UPDATE
To date we have researched various methods of removing the native bullrushes growing in
the Birdsville Billabong. Options considered include excavating with a machine, poisoning
with chemicals, or burning.
Advice was sought from Elders, who supply most of Council chemicals requirements, on
which chemicals would be suitable for using to destroy the bullrush without any harm to the
existing flora, fauna and fish in the Diamantina River. Elders responded that they would not
recommend using any chemicals which could damage the environment, as they have had
issues in the past (see attached email).
We are looking at other sources for supply of chemicals. Barcaldine Council have used a
contractor to spray their bullrush, and we are waiting to receive information of the contractor
they used. Once we have received the contact details, we will make contact and see if they
can assist us with removing the bullrush.
A plan is in place to meet with Birdsville Rural Fire Services and Queensland Police to see if
it is possible to undertake a burn, after the events season is over. This meeting is booked for
2.00pm, 18 September 2024.
We have been in touch with Wesley Philips, Environmental Officer for RAPAD, for any
information he may have, to assist us with the eradication of bullrushes in the Diamantina
River, Birdsville. At the time of writing, we are still awaiting his response.

          the actual delivery time exceeds the stated delivery time. Council also reserves
          the power to subtract this calculated penalty amount from the Tender price and

CONDITIONS OF REQUEST FOR TENDER FOR MOTOR VEHICLES
1.1 Request for Tender Documents
      A. The Organisation providing the Tender shall complete all details on the Tender
         Form which shall be recognised as the Tender.
      B. The Organisation providing the Tender shall sign the Tender or if the
         Organisation is a corporation, affix the common seal or otherwise formally sign
         the Tender.
      C. Selection shall be made from the signed Tender and not from any literature or
         letter accompanying the Tender, unless such attachments are specifically
         referred to in the signed Tender Schedule.


1.2 Variations from Specification
      A. If because of the basic design or other factors it is impracticable for the
           organisation providing the Tender to fully comply with the specifications of the
           vehicle required, he/she shall clearly list these variations and attach to the
           General Request for Tender Schedule.
      B. Unless these exclusions are stated, it shall be expected that the vehicle offered
           complies with the specification in all respects.


1.3 Time for Delivery
       A. The organisation providing the Tender shall state on the tender the time for
          delivery of the vehicles. A monetary penalty shall be incurred by the successful
          organisation on failure to comply with the stated time, and at Council discretion.
          The penalty shall be calculated at the rate of 0.1% of the Tender price per
          ordinary working day, i.e., Monday to Friday, exclusive of public holidays, that
          the actual delivery time exceeds the stated delivery time. Council also reserves
          the power to subtract this calculated penalty amount from the Tender price and
          to make payment accordingly.
       B. Delivery shall be to the Council Depot at Eyre Street, Bedourie, and the supplying
          organisation should nominate the price involved in delivering the item to this
          point in their Tender price. If the successful organisation/supplier fails to supply
          the vehicles or equipment quoted within the time set out in their Tender
          document, Council reserves the right to cancel the order and either place an
          order with another organisation/supplier or recall Tenders.




Agenda Ordinary Council Meeting Monday 16 September 2024                               Page 243
1.4 Lodgement of Tender
      A. The Tender must be lodged thorough the Vendor panel system.

1.5      Acceptance of Quotation
      A. Any Tender which does not comply with the requirements of the conditions of
         quoting in all respects may be rejected.
      B. The lowest Tender may not necessarily be accepted
      C. The organisation whose Tender has been approved and accepted shall be advised by
         the placement of an official order form from Council.
      D. If the successful organisation fails to supply the vehicles quoted on within the time
         as set out in their Tender documents, Council reserves the right to cancel the order
         and either place an order with another organisation or recall the quotations.

1. Summary
Audit progress – Behind Schedule
We have completed our audit planning processes and interim audit.

 Financial reporting risks and areas of audit focus
 We have commenced our audit procedures over the areas of audit focus that we identified in the external
 audit plan. For these areas, we have held meetings with management within key business areas to
 understand any new business updates, and to confirm the design and implementation of key financial
 reporting controls.
 Council has experienced significant change of executive leadership in the preceding two years, including
 the CEO. There have been 8 CEO’s in permanent and acting roles since August 2022. At the time of our
 interim audit, Scott Mason, a former Council CEO (2007 – 2013) had been appointed as Interim CEO.
 Recruitment of a permanent CEO is in progress.
 The audit report for FY 2023 was signed 31 January 2024 and Council is behind in financial reporting for FY
 2024.
 Scott Mason has been working closely with the newly elected Council on implementing a “financial
 turnaround strategy”. This process involves working to re-build the organisational capability of Council,
 particularly with respect to financial and management reporting. To this end, a team of consultants (some
 with prior experience with Council), are working to review and revise Council’s policies and procedures.
 Council are heavily involved in this process and a number of workshops have been conducted.
 Whilst Council is currently behind schedule in its financial reporting, there is confidence with the team in
 place and a concerted effort, that statutory timeframes for FY 2024 will be met.

  3 June 2024                          pro forma financial statements due (behind schedule )

 $274,000 overall materiality
 Based on our work to date, which included a walkthrough of key control processes to assess design and
 implementation of your controls, we have not identified any new control deficiencies or financial reporting
 issues.

 valuations in our closing letter in October 2024.

4. Update on new reports and resources
 We present to you our update on reports and resources, as at 30 June 2024. It provides an overview of the
 information relevant to your entity, including learnings from our tabled reports to parliament, newly published
 resources such as our blog articles and fact sheets, and an update on our audits that are in progress.


Forward work plan
QAO’s forward work plan for 2024–27 is now available. Our plan provides our expected audit activity for the
next 3 years in response to the strategic risks facing public sector entities and local governments. Our
upcoming audits cover a broad range of government services. Auditing the right matters at the right time is key
for ensuring we add value for the entities we engage with, and to ensure our work drives positive change. Our
plan includes 6 focus areas for the coming year:
    •    Technology risk and opportunities
    •    Sustainable communities and environment
    •    Governance of government
    •    Healthy and safe Queenslanders
    •    Infrastructure investment
    •    Economic risk and response.
We also provide an acquittal with the plan outlining any changes to the topics, timing, or audit scope from the
previous year’s plan.
Read the full plan at Forward work plan 2024–27. Topics that may be of interest to you are in the table below.




   Agenda Ordinary Council Meeting Monday 16 September 2024                                                   Page 270
 Tabling year                                                       Audit

2024–25           Reducing landfill waste
                  This audit will assess the effectiveness of state government strategies for reducing landfill waste. This
                  will include assessing:
                  •   how effective local governments are in implementing the state government’s strategies
                  •   how effective the state government is in assisting local governments to manage waste to achieve
                      relevant targets.

2025–26           Managing third party cyber security risks
                  This audit will examine how effectively public sector entities:
                  •   identify third parties who have access to their data and network
                  •   assess the security vulnerabilities the entity is exposed to through third parties
                  •   establish relevant controls to manage third party cyber security risks
                  •   minimise the impact of third-party security breaches.

                  Mitigating risk from future floods
                  Flooding causes more damage in Queensland than any other natural disaster. The estimated social,
                  financial, and economic cost to Queensland of the 2022 floods was $7.7 billion.
                  This audit will assess how the government is planning and preparing for future floods by mitigating the
                  risk associated with these events.

                  Enhancing sustainability of local governments
                  This audit will be the fifth in a series of local government sustainability audits that we have undertaken.
                  It will examine the sector’s progress in meeting its sustainability challenges.
                  It will assess how effectively the sector has acted to address previous QAO findings and
                  recommendations.

2026–27           Managing volunteer services
                  This audit will assess whether the government is effectively managing its volunteer workforce (for
                  example, the Rural Fire Service and State Emergency Service). The audit may consider issues such
                  as workforce attraction and retention.

                  Planning for liveable communities
                  This audit will assess how the Queensland Government’s planning framework supports economic
                  growth and development and liveability. We will also examine how effectively the state and local
                  governments collaborate and coordinate their long-term plans to provide the services needed to
                  support Queensland’s growing population.

Recently tabled reports to parliament
Since your last meeting, we have tabled the below reports to parliament. For more information on any of these
reports, please see our website: www.qao.qld.gov.au/reports-resources/reports-parliament.

 Report                                                                  Summary

 Reducing serious youth            Youth crime is complex and has been a growing public concern in recent years. It can
 crime                             have significant impacts – physical, emotional, psychological, and economical – for
 Report 15: 2023–24                victims and the wider community. Most young offenders only commit a small number
 Tabled 28 June 2024               of offences and are diverted away from the youth justice system. However, a small
                                   proportion reoffend and commit serious offences. As the underlying causes of youth
                                   crime are multi-faceted, effectively addressing the problem requires a whole-of-system
                                   approach.
                                   This report assesses whether youth justice strategies and programs are effective in
                                   reducing crime by serious repeat offenders and improving community safety:
                                   www.qao.qld.gov.au/reports-resources/reports-parliament/reducing-serious-youth-
                                   crime
                                   Wider learnings
                                   Multi-agency delivery and coordination
                                   Delivering government initiatives in a multi-agency operating model is inherently
                                   challenging. Entities typically have their own mandates, objectives, and leadership
                                   structures. To be successful, entities need clearly defined strategies, roles, and
                                   responsibilities, with coordination and oversight requiring effective cross-entity
                                   governance. Entities should commit to these models while ensuring a focus on both
                                   entity level and multi-entity strategies. They must be open to sharing information and
                                   collaborating, while maintaining focus on joint outcomes.
                                   Procurement and contract management practices
                                   Entities should base procurement decisions on sound needs and analysis. To achieve
                                   value for money, they should be regularly testing the market. They should sufficiently
                                   maintain documentation to help support their analysis and decisions. When engaging
                                   contractors, they need to include sufficient performance measures and targets within
                                   contracts, with a focus on both outputs and outcomes.
                                   Monitoring and evaluating the effectiveness of strategies and programs
                                   Entities should continuously evaluate the effectiveness of their strategies and
                                   programs. This must be informed by:
                                   •   the design and monitoring of clear and measurable performance indicators
                                   •   regular, ongoing monitoring, evaluation and reporting.
                                   It is crucial they have systems and processes in place to capture necessary data.
                                   Informed analysis, and measuring performance, can improve decision making. It also
                                   enables entities to adapt their strategies to changing circumstances.

 Queensland’s regions 2023         Queensland is the second largest state in Australia and has the most people living
 Report 14: 2023–24                outside greater capital city areas. Queensland’s regions (referring to all areas outside
                                   Greater Brisbane) cover around 99 per cent of the state. It ranges from coastal cities,
 Tabled 13 June 2024
                                   like the Gold Coast, through to the Far North, to more remote outback areas. Our
                                   regions are home to diverse regional economies and environments, reflected in
                                   significant industries like mining, manufacturing, agriculture, and tourism.
                                   This report brings together insights from our financial audits across entities, and
                                   analyses data on state and local government service delivery and support to the
                                   state’s regions: www.qao.qld.gov.au/reports-resources/reports-
                                   parliament/queenslands-regions-2023
                                   Wider learnings




   Agenda Ordinary Council Meeting Monday 16 September 2024                                                  Page 272
Report                                                                  Summary
                                 •   Entities may need to adapt their plans and services to accommodate changing
                                     community needs.
                                 •   Having useful data is important for measuring the success of policy initiatives.
                                     Without it, entities cannot accurately track their progress against objectives.
                                 •   Entities across government must work together to effectively deliver initiatives,
                                     including working across internal boundaries, having clear roles and
                                     responsibilities for each entity, and implementing appropriate governance
                                     arrangements. Entities may need to contribute some of their own resources to
                                     achieve a common goal.

Responding to and                The nature, frequency, and severity of cyber attacks continues to grow and evolve.
recovering from cyber            Public sector and local government entities, regardless of size or location, are a target
attacks                          because of what they do and the type of information they hold. Cyber incidents may
Report 12: 2023–24               compromise entities’ information systems and business operations –significantly
Tabled 4 June 2024               disrupting the delivery of critical public services. This can have long-lasting economic
                                 and social impacts. All entities need to proactively manage their cyber security risks,
                                 identify vulnerabilities, and ensure they can respond to an incident.
                                 This report discusses how prepared public sector entities are to respond to and
                                 recover from cyber security incidents. We examined 2 lead entities and their role in
                                 guiding cyber security across the Queensland Government, and 3 other entities with
                                 differing levels of resourcing and capability for managing cyber incidents:
                                 www.qao.qld.gov.au/reports-resources/reports-parliament/responding-recovering-
                                 cyber-attacks
                                 We have published 2 better practice guides. Our checklist of key questions for those
                                 charged with governance (executive management, boards, and councillors) to
                                 consider when planning how they respond to and recover from cyber security
                                 incidents: www.qao.qld.gov.au/reports-resources/better-practice/cyber-response-
                                 recovery-governance-checklist. And a checklist for entities to map where they do or do
                                 not hold cyber capabilities: www.qao.qld.gov.au/reports-resources/better-practice/role-
                                 capability-checklist-cyber-attack-response-recovery.
                                 Wider learnings
                                 Take a business-led approach to cyber incident response
                                 Responding to a cyber attack requires a coordinated approach across the business. It
                                 is not simply a technical exercise. This ‘business-led approach’ focuses on the
                                 broader organisational impacts of a cyber incident rather than just the technical cyber
                                 and systems elements. Entities should bring key stakeholders such as legal,
                                 communications, and operational areas in with management and technical teams to
                                 coordinate the response.
                                 Periodically test preparedness
                                 Entities need to test their preparedness for managing and responding to cyber
                                 attacks. Just having plans in place is not sufficient. Testing these plans through
                                 exercises such as cyber simulations:
                                 •   provides entities with valuable feedback on how they are managing risks and
                                     identifying vulnerabilities, and helps them identify any areas requiring improvement
                                 •   gives key personnel experience in managing these incidents in a safe
                                     environment.
                                 Take ownership of third-party cyber-related risks
                                 Those charged with governance at public sector entities and local governments need
                                 to understand and be accountable for all of their cyber risks. Most entities have
                                 arrangements in place with third-party providers, which includes access to systems
                                 and to expertise and resources. Entities must understand risks that arise under these
                                 arrangements and be accountable for managing them.
                                 Collaborate and share learnings
                                 Most entities face similar cyber risks and use similar products, networks, hardware,
                                 systems, and applications. As such, it is critical that entities proactively share their
                                 knowledge and lessons learned, and collaborate to improve their preparedness. All
                                 entities should take part in central communities of practice and forums available to
                                 them, such as those the Queensland Government Cyber Security Unit leads.


 Agenda Ordinary Council Meeting Monday 16 September 2024                                                    Page 273
 Report                                                                  Summary
                                   Evolve alongside changing cyber risks
                                   The changing nature of technology means that cyber security threats evolve rapidly.
                                   The development of new technologies, such as artificial intelligence and machine-
                                   learning, compounds this. Entities need to continually revisit and refresh their plans
                                   and risk assessments to ensure they are prepared for a cyber attack.
                                   Recommendations for all entities
                                   We made a series of detailed recommendations to all entities. In summary, we
                                   recommended that all entities:
                                   1.   protect their systems and sensitive information
                                   2.   formally recognise in key governance documents that responsibility for cyber
                                        security rests with the chief executive, or equivalent
                                   3.   improve and test incident response plans
                                   4.   improve their crisis communication plans and templates
                                   5.   gain access to the technical skills required to respond to and recover from cyber
                                        incidents
                                   6.   share cyber threat intelligence and lessons learnt with the Queensland
                                        Government cyber security unit (CSU) and other public sector entities as quickly
                                        as possible.
                                   We also recommended that local governments document their assessment on
                                   whether IS18:2018 is appropriate to their environments, and if not, which frameworks
                                   are being applied to manage information security risks.
                                   The full recommendations are in our report. The council should assess these
                                   recommendations and action any that apply to them.

Insights from other jurisdictions: Cyber security in local government
Background
Similar to the QAO, the Audit Office of New South Wales (NSW AO) reports to parliament over the years have
highlighted gaps in councils' cyber security risk management approaches since 2019.
Their Local Government 2023 report, tabled in March 2024, found that 50 councils were yet to implement cyber
security governance frameworks and related internal controls.
In a recently published report on cyber security in local government, the NSW AO undertook a deep dive into 3
councils and assessed how effectively they identified and managed cyber security risks.

Findings in this report that relate to councils
1. Ineffective identification and managing of cyber risk
• Risk management processes did not identify and manage cyber risk.
• Governance arrangements in managing and reporting cyber security risks were ineffective.
• Value of the information assets and systems were not assessed to inform the risk councils are exposed to.
• Policies and procedures to manage cyber risk were ineffective and there were no plans to improve their
  cyber security.

   Agenda Ordinary Council Meeting Monday 16 September 2024                                                  Page 274
• There is no clear and consistent approach to monitoring the effectiveness of controls to mitigate identified
  cyber security risks.
2. Lack of up-to-date plans and processes to support effective detection, response, and recovery from
   cyber security incidents
• Lack of cyber incident response plans to ensure an effective response to and prompt recovery from cyber
  incidents.
• Out-of-date business continuity and disaster recovery planning.
• No clearly defined roles and responsibilities for detecting, responding to, and recovering from cyber
  incidents.
• No register of cyber incidents was maintained to record information about the sources and types of incidents
  experienced and relevant responses, to support post-incident evaluation.

Recommendations to New South Wales councils in this report
• Integrate the assessment and monitoring of cyber security risks into corporate governance processes.
• Complete a self-assessment against the foundational requirements in the Cyber Security Guidelines – Local
  Government and report the results to audit committees.
• Implement a plan and program to improve cyber security.
• Develop, implement, and test a cyber incident response plan.

What can Queensland councils take away from this report?
1. Undertake a self-assessment of your council’s practices against the NSW's Cyber Security Guidelines –
   Local Government to identify any improvement opportunities.
2. Discuss the results of the self-assessment with your audit committees and elected members.

                              30TH JUNE 2024 STOCK TAKE WRITE-OFF IMPACT



BACKGROUND:

An annual stock take is required to be performed as of 30 June and any required adjustments are to be
processed in accordance with the relevant accounting standards. This report brieﬁng is to report to
council the ﬁnancial impact of this process being reduction of $379,383.57 in stores value as at 30
June 2024.

ISSUES IDENTIFIED:

During the end of the ﬁnancial year stores clean up and stock take process several issues where
identiﬁed which had an impact of the amount processed to the Stores & Purchasing Write-
o s/Adjustments general ledger account. These issues included but not limited to the following:

      The stores Stock Cost File report having many historical transactions that had not been
       cleared out for a number of years.
      Store codes being duplicated with transactions but no stock location
      Errors in stock counts entered for FY 2022/23.
      Large volume of inactive/obsolete stock items currently in the stock valuation.
      Some stock items being unable to be located during the stock count process.



IMPACT:

   1. The Stock Cost File report should only contain current transactions for which a stock receipt
      has been processed or a creditor payment has been made for stock items that have not yet had
      the stock receival processed. The system automatically removes matched transactions from
      the report as they are processed. However, if the two transactions do not accurately match,
      they will continue to report until a manual process is performed to match the transactions o .
      These transactions impact the average unit cost of the associated store items and stock on
      hand quantities. As part of the 23/24 stores clean-up project a large number of adjustments for
      historical transactions were manually processed in the system. The total value of these
      adjustments was $121,994.20.




       Agenda Ordinary Council Meeting Monday 16 September 2024                         Page 285

   stock counts applied previously particularly for duplicated store codes with no stock location.

   stock write-o adjustments of greater than $10,000. The total of these adjustments is

      are marked as Inactive or Obsolete. The value of these items is $148,616.72.

The values of points 1 and 2 above total $355,676.26 of the total adjustment amount of $379,383.57.
The Inactive items totalling $148,616.72 currently remain in the stock system.


RECOMMENDATIONS:

   1. That the stock adjustment amount of $379,383.57 be approved for write o .

   2. That the Stock Cost File report be reviewed and required adjustments processed monthly and
      signed o on by management.

   3. That the stock valuation report be run monthly and reviewed. In particular, the average unit
      cost be reviewed for obvious anomalies.

   4. That Locations be established in Stock system to allow small periodic stocktakes to be
      performed throughout the year. This will ensure that count variances and discrepancies are
      identiﬁed and rectiﬁed on a timely basis.

   5. That inactive/obsolete store items be removed from the system and either o ered for sale or
      disposed of.

   6. That the Unused Stock Report be used periodically to identify stock items that have not been
      moved after a speciﬁc date. This report could be used to identify store items that need to be
      removed from the system and potentially be o ered for sale.

12.3.1 BIRDSVILLE RACES – POST EVENT REPORT
 Directorate:                             Chief Operating Officer
 Date:                                    16 September 2024
 To:                                      Ordinary Council Meeting
 Author:                                  Jason Beaton, Chief Operating Officer
 Authorising Officer:                     Scott Mason, Interim Chief Executive Officer
 File Reference:                          IX


OFFICER RECOMMENDATION
That Council receive the Birdsville Races – Post Event Report and that those matters not
covered by resolution be noted.


ATTACHMENTS
    1. 2024 Birdsville Races - Post Event Report
OPERATIONAL UPDATE
Purpose
To provide Council with a post-event overview of the 2024 Birdsville Races, held on 6–7
September 2024, including key outcomes, challenges, and recommendations for future
events. The summary of the report is as follows:
Overview
The 2024 Birdsville Races attracted approximately 3,000 attendees, marking another
successful year for this iconic event. Minimal incidents were reported, and feedback from
stakeholders was largely positive. Several recommendations and improvements were noted
to enhance future event planning and execution.
Key points include:
    •    Strong communication between the Race Club and Council, with regular stakeholder
         meetings recommended for future events.
    •    A proposal to create a more vibrant festival atmosphere, with alternative
         entertainment options being explored.
SWOT Analysis for Birdsville Races
Strengths:
    •    Well-known event with a strong reputation in tourism.
    •    Positive relationships with both the Race Club and community stakeholders.
Weaknesses:
    •    Low staffing levels led to operational challenges.
    •    Internal communication between Council departments was not fully streamlined.




Agenda Ordinary Council Meeting Monday 16 September 2024                                 Page 369
    •    Shuttle buses and accessible toilet/shower facilities at Tent City were identified as
         areas for improvement.
Opportunities:
    •    Promoting the event and Birdsville through a central hub in Burt Street with music
         and entertainment.
    •    Expanding the parade and growing the festival’s appeal.
    •    Establishing an Event Control Centre for better coordination.
Threats:
    •    Decreasing attendance numbers pose a long-term risk.
    •    Adverse weather conditions could affect the event.
    •    Staff burnout and lack of clear processes were concerns, particularly with managing
         workloads and lighting issues at the oval.


Road Closures
Road closures were well-managed, with positive feedback from emergency services and the
community. Some areas for improvement include:
    •    The need for reduced-speed signs in shard zones.
    •    Increasing the number of shuttle buses for better management of crowd flow during
         track egress and pub closing times.


Public Safety
Public safety was a top priority, particularly given the extreme heat experienced during the
event. Water distribution at race track gates helped keep attendees hydrated while waiting
for shuttle buses. The assistance of clinic nurses and other personnel was commendable.
Recommendations:
    •    Council should purchase a pallet of 250ml water bottles for future events.
    •    Investigate the installation of taps and misters at the race track gates for continuous
         water supply and cooling.


Rent-a-Tent
The Rent-a-Tent service operated smoothly, though there is room for improvement in
messaging and layout. Earlier communication about available packages and designated
camping areas is recommended. Premium unpowered camping options at the end of the
oval should be explored for future events.




Agenda Ordinary Council Meeting Monday 16 September 2024                                  Page 370
Vendors
The layout and power infrastructure for vendor areas need to be reassessed. Creating a
central entertainment hub and selecting specific vendors through an EOI process will
enhance the vendor experience and event appeal.


Parks, Gardens, and Tourism Team
Feedback was overwhelmingly positive regarding the cleanliness of public facilities and the
helpfulness of Council staff. Visiting QPS and QAS teams commended the Council’s
professionalism.


General Observations:
    •    Additional seating near the Wirrarri Centre should be cleaned prior to events.
    •    Maintenance forms should be completed for event showers before and after the
         event.
    •    Additional wheelie bins are required at Rent-a-Tent areas, and skip bins on the
         common were effective.


Recommendations:
    •    Close Burt Street between Florence and Adelaide Streets for event duration to
         manage traffic.
    •    Open the vendor area for a full week with set trading times and fees.
    •    Review Rent-a-Tent layout and provide additional 3x3 and 6x3 marquees for shade
         and shelter.
    •    Increase shuttle bus capacity to four buses.
    •    Install misters and water taps at race track gates for cooling and hydration.
    •    Engage a Public Safety/Risk Management contractor, such as ERMS Group, for
         future events.

         4. Public Safety

     Public Safety is, as defined in the Public Safety Preservation Act 1986, “the provision of
     protection for members of the public in terrorist, chemical, biological, radiological or other
     emergencies that create or may create danger of death, injury or distress to any person, loss
     of or damage to any property or pollution of the environment and for related purposes”
     It was discussed and arranged between Patrice (DSC) and Stephan (QPS) the weekend
     prior due to the extreme heat the region had been experiencing, the lack of shade at the
     gates and the length of time it takes to clear under public safety the Provision of additional
     water for Egress at Race Track and the following amount of water was purchased;

            2 x 10ltr
            5x 6x1.5ltr bottles
            2 x 20x250ml bottles
            5 pkts of small cups
     This with the water coolers that were at the gates aided in keeping the race patrons hydrated
     whilst waiting for the shuttle buses.
     The water was being handed out by all available emergency services, security, council
     personnel. The additional assistance from the Clinic nurses was fantastic on Saturday.
     Recommendation

            DSC to purchase water for the event to be handed out, recommend purchasing a
             pallet of the 250ml bottles.
            Also investigate the installation of taps at the gate of the track to enable the
             installation of misters and continuous water.
